fullName: RansomLook contains multiple weaknesses in its authentication endpoint that allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to enumerate valid usernames, perform unrestricted password-guessing attacks, and potentially exhaust application worker re
normalized: cve 2026 78551 ransomlook contains multiple weaknesses in its authentication endpoint that allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to enumerate valid usernames perform unrestricted password guessing attacks and potentially exhaust application worker resources for local authentication the login implementation previously checked whether a submitted username existed before invoking the password hash verification function requests containing a nonexistent username therefore returned significantly faster than requests for valid accounts for which the computationally expensive password verification routine was executed a remote attacker could measure these response time differences to determine which usernames correspond to valid ransomlook accounts in addition the login endpoint did not restrict the number or frequency of failed authentication attempts an attacker could consequently perform password brute force dictionary password spraying or credential stuffing attacks against known accounts without server side throttling for valid usernames each authentication attempt also invokes the password key derivation function which consumes a significant amount of cpu time a sufficiently high rate of login attempts could therefore occupy the application s synchronous gunicorn workers and cause a denial of service affecting the entire application the issue has been addressed by always performing password verification using a randomly generated dummy password hash when the supplied username does not exist eliminating the username dependent timing discrepancy failed authentication attempts are additionally rate limited per client ip address using valkey redis with five failed attempts within five minutes resulting in a one hour block the reverse proxy configuration was also updated so that the application derives the client address from a trusted x forwarded for value that cannot be overridden by a client supplied header

fullName: RansomLook exposed complete API keys in the HTML source of the authenticated /admin/apikeys administration page.

fullName: An out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in the streaming RPC client of Apache bRPC (versions 1.11.0 through  1.17.0) on all platforms.
normalized: cve 2026 79704 an out of bounds read vulnerability exists in the streaming rpc client of apache brpc versions 1 11 0 through 1 17 0 on all platforms a client that creates multiple streams in a single rpc expects the server response to carry exactly one extra stream id for every additional stream the response handling path indexed the returned identifiers using the locally created stream count without first validating the size of the returned list so a malicious or compromised server or an on path attacker can trigger an out of bounds read in the client by returning a malformed streamsettings response with fewer extra stream ids than expected this may crash the client process denial of service or leak unintended memory contents into subsequent stream handling surplus identifiers have no valid client stream mapping and are processed inconsistently root cause since brpc 1 11 0 a client can create multiple streams in one rpc via batch streamcreate the expected behavior is that the server response must return exactly n 1 extra stream ids where n is the number of locally created streams in controller handlestreamconnection the response path reads extra stream ids i 1 for each additional local stream without first comparing the returned list size with n 1 if the server returns fewer identifiers the read runs past the end of the returned list out of bounds read if it returns more the surplus identifiers have no corresponding client side stream affected scenarios a brpc client using multi stream rpc creating more than one stream in a single rpc that connects to an untrusted malicious or compromised server or to a server reached through an untrusted network path the server sends a malformed streamsettings response to trigger the issue how to fix choose one of the following options 1 upgrade brpc to version 1 18 0 which fixes this issue 2 apply this patch https github com apache brpc pull 3485 note the fix makes the client reject responses whose extra stream ids count does not exactly match the number of additional client streams such mismatched responses now fail the rpc with eresponse and go through the existing stream cleanup path instead of being partially processed
